title: How a Sick Chicken Revolutionized Cancer Research - Nautilus
gist: A review in Genes & Cancer recounts how Francis Peyton Rous, at the Rockefeller Institute in 1909, used a Barred Plymouth Rock hen's tumor to show viruses can cause cancer. The discovery was initially dismissed but is now well-established.

insights.claim: Viruses can cause cancer, a now well-established fact whose discovery was initially dismissed by the scientific community.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: A reminder that initially-dismissed science can later reshape a field, such as oncology and vaccine-based prevention.
insights.quote: Viruses can cause cancer. It’s something that’s well-established now, but the discovery was initially dismissed by the scientific community.

insights.claim: A new review published in Genes & Cancer tells the story of Francis Peyton Rous, the scientist credited with the discovery.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie

insights.claim: In 1909, while Rous was studying cancer at the Rockefeller Institute, a chicken farmer brought him a Barred Plymouth Rock hen with a large breast tumor, which led to work that altered cancer research.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Illustrates serendipity in breakthrough biomedical research.
insights.locator: Rous was working at the Rockefeller
